statement: The curve $x^{3}+y^{3}=3axy$ (folium of Descartes) has $a>0$. (i) Find $\\frac{dy}{dx}$ by implicit differentiation. (ii) Show that at the point where $x=y$ (with $x\\neq 0$) the tangent has gradient $-1$ and find its equation.
solution: (i) Differentiating: $3x^{2}+3y^{2}y'=3a(y+xy')$, so $y'=\\frac{ay-x^{2}}{y^{2}-ax}$. (ii) At $x=y$: $x^{3}+x^{3}=3ax^{2}\\Rightarrow 2x^{3}=3ax^{2}\\Rightarrow x=3a/2$ (nonzero). Then $y'=\\frac{a x-x^{2}}{x^{2}-ax}=-1$. Point $(3a/2,3a/2)$; tangent: $y-3a/2=-(x-3a/2)$, i.e. $x+y=3a$.
hints: Differentiate both sides with respect to $x$.
